title: Sanctions against Amanda Nightingale (née Cleaver)
text:
1
Edited for publication
WITHOUT PREJUDICE
IN THE MATTER OF
THE EXECUTIVE COUNSEL TO THE FINANCIAL REPORTING COUNCIL
-and-
AMANDA NIGHTINGALE (NÉE CLEAVER)

SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT

The Settlement Agreement (which includes the Particulars of Fact and Acts of Misconduct) is a
document agreed between Amanda Nightingale and the Executive Counsel. It does not make
findings against any persons other than Ms Nightingale and it would not be fair to treat any
part of this document as constituting findings against any other persons.
1. This Settlement Agreement (“Agreement”) is made on 11 June 2024 between Jamie
Symington as Deputy Executive Counsel of the Financial Reporting Council (“the
Executive Counsel”), and Ms Amanda Nightingale (together “the Parties”). The
Agreement is evidenced by the signatures of the Parties.
2. The Parties recognise that the determination to be made in this case is a matter for the
Tribunal member in accordance with paragraph 8(4)(ii) of the FRC Accountancy
Scheme (“the Scheme”).
3. Terms used in this Agreement shall have the same meaning as set out in the Scheme
and the FRC Sanctions Guidance dated March 2021 (“the 2021 Sanctions
Guidance”).
4. If the decision is to approve the Agreement, including the sanctions set out below, then
the Agreement shall take effect from the next working day after the date on which the
notice of the decision is sent to the Parties in accordance with paragraph 8(4)(iv) of
the Scheme.

5. The Particulars of Fact and Acts of Misconduct against Amanda Nightingale ("the
Particulars”) as a former member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England
and Wales (“ICAEW”) were prepared by the Executive Counsel and agreed by the
Parties in accordance with the Scheme and are annexed at Annex 1.
6. The Particulars are in respect of Ms Nightingale’s conduct whilst employed by BDO
LLP as a Senior Manager. On numerous occasions between 2015 and 2019, the

2
conduct of Ms Nightingale fell significantly short of the standards reasonably to be
expected of a Member and has brought, or is likely to bring, discredit to herself, BDO
and to the accountancy profession in that she:
a. caused or permitted auditor’s reports to be issued without approval from the
Responsible Individuals, including by inserting electronic copies of the signature of
the Responsible Individual for the relevant audit without their authorisation;
b. inserted electronic copies of the signatures of the Responsible Individuals in other
documents, including company accounts which she then filed at Companies
House, without their authorisation;
c. created false documents, and falsified existing documents, including audit
evidence; and
d. deceived the Responsible Individuals and audited entities.
7. Ms Nightingale admits the Particulars and the 49 Allegations contained within it.
Sanction
8. The Parties have agreed the following terms of settlement in respect of sanction for
Ms Nightingale’s Misconduct:

a. Ms Nightingale be excluded from the ICAEW for a recommended period of 20
years;
b. A Condition that Ms Nightingale shall not undertake any accountancy work for a
period of 20 years, defined as:

acting as a “professional accountant in public practice” or a “professional
accountant in business” as defined in the glossary of the ICAEW Code of
Ethics1;

the matters defined as “public practice” by the ICAEW ‘Definition of public
practice’ guidance2;

being involved in preparing or signing financial statements, save as they relate
solely to her personal financial affairs;

performing any financial roles in the operation of a business, including but not
limited to: Chief Financial Officer, Finance Director, Group Finance Director,
Financial Controller, Finance Manager, Divisional Director of Finance; and

holding herself out as a member of the ICAEW, or as a person capable of
carrying out the above-listed accountancy work.

c. a published statement, in the form of a Severe Reprimand

1 See definition in Annex 1 and https://www.icaew.com/-/media/corporate/files/members/regulations-
standards-and-guidance/ethics/icaew-code-of-ethics-2020.ashx?la=en#page=193
2 See definition in Annex 2 and https://www.icaew.com/technical/practice-resources/regulations-standards-
guidance-and-ethics/definition-of-public-practice

3
9. In determining the appropriate sanctions against Ms Nightingale, the Executive
Counsel adopted the approach set out in paragraph 18 of the 2021 Sanctions
Guidance, as follows:

Nature and Seriousness of the Misconduct
10. The Executive Counsel considers that the factors relevant to assessing the nature and
seriousness of the Misconduct are:
a. The Misconduct in this case was of a very serious nature and involved forgery of
audit reports, the creation of false documents, falsifying existing documents and
deception of Responsible Individuals and audited entities.
b. The Misconduct involved a failure to comply with important professional standards.
The standards breached, including the Fundamental Principles of Integrity and
Professional Behaviour, are critical to upholding trust and public confidence in the
accountancy profession. The Misconduct also involved a failure to comply with the
requirements of s503 of the Companies Act 2006, which is further damaging to
public confidence in statutory audit.
c. The Misconduct was intentional and dishonest but it does not appear that any
financial gain was derived or intended to be derived from the Misconduct other than
her remuneration from BDO for performing professional services which she did not
perform to the required standard as detailed in the Particulars. The motivation for
the Misconduct remains unclear but certain of Ms Nightingale’s personal
circumstances have been taken into account as set out in the mitigating factors.
d. The scale and significance of the Misconduct was substantial. It was repeated on
numerous occasions, across numerous audits and occurred over a number of
years.
e. The Misconduct is likely to undermine confidence in the standards of conduct in
general of Members and Member Firms and financial reporting and in the
profession generally.
f. It is not alleged that the Misconduct caused or risked the loss of significant sums
of money or adversely affected or potentially adversely affected a significant
number of people in the United Kingdom given the nature and size of the audited
entities to which it relates.
g. The Executive Counsel cannot be confident that the same type of Misconduct will
not recur absent Ms Nightingale’s exclusion from the ICAEW and a Condition that
she does not undertake accountancy work for a very significant period.
Identification of Sanction

11. Having assessed the seriousness of the Misconduct and considered the range of
available sanctions, the Executive Counsel considers that the sanctions identified
above are appropriate.

4
12. Pursuant to paragraph 51 of the 2021 Sanctions Guidance, the Executive Counsel
considers that Exclusion from the ICAEW and the Condition not to undertake
accountancy work are necessary. The removal of Ms Nightingale’s professional status
is the most appropriate outcome in order to protect the public and safeguard the public
interest in circumstances where the Misconduct is so damaging to the wider public and
market confidence in the standards of conducts of Members and in the accountancy
profession.
13. For the avoidance of doubt, the Executive Counsel has considered all other available
sanctions and whether an Exclusion and the Condition are the most appropriate
sanctions and has concluded that they are given, among other things, the Misconduct
in this case is fundamentally incompatible with continued membership of the ICAEW
and the undertaking of accountancy work.
14. Further, the Executive Counsel has determined it is also appropriate to impose a
Severe Reprimand given the scale and gravity of the Misconduct identified.
15. The Executive Counsel has determined that it is not necessary to impose a financial
sanction in this matter having had regard to the factors listed at paragraph 33 of the
2021 Sanctions Guidance. Namely, Ms Nightingale does not appear to have derived
any financial gain or benefit as a result of the Misconduct, the Misconduct does not
appear to have involved or caused the loss of significant sums of money and, in view
of the unique and unprecedented nature of the Misconduct, there are no obvious
similar previous cases where a Fine was imposed.
16. Further, the Executive Counsel considers that the aims and objectives of the Scheme
and of sanctions as set out in paragraph 9 of the 2021 Sanctions Guidance can be
fulfilled without the imposition of a financial sanction. The Executive Counsel considers
that the exceptional period of Exclusion imposed on Ms Nightingale, together with the
onerous terms of the Condition and the Severe Reprimand are very grave sanctions,
the personal and financial effects of which will be very significant. Taking the package
of sanctions as a whole, Executive Counsel considers that they will declare and uphold
proper standards among Members, maintain and promote public and market
confidence in the accountancy profession, appropriately protect the public and act as
a sufficient deterrent.
17. The Executive Counsel has taken into account aggravating and mitigating factors as
set out below. The Executive Counsel has concluded that the sanctions set out in
paragraph 8 above are appropriate, and no adjustment to sanctions is necessary,
having regard to the purpose of the Scheme.
18. Further, having regard to paragraph 72 of the 2021 Sanctions Guidance, which states
that it will not normally be inappropriate to reduce the period which a Member is to be
precluded from practising to reflect a settlement because the primary purpose of such
a sanction is to protect the public, the Executive Counsel has concluded no discount
for settlement is appropriate.
Aggravating Factors

5
19. No aggravating factors which have not already been taken into account in the
assessment of seriousness have been identified.
Mitigating Factors
20. The following mitigating factors were identified:

a. Ms Nightingale has personal mitigating circumstances in that a close family
member suffered serious ill-health throughout the material period and that, in
conjunction with her full-time role as a senior manager in a large audit firm, this
placed very significant mental and physical burdens upon her.

b. Ms Nightingale has apologised and shown contrition for the Misconduct.
Deterrence
21. The Executive Counsel does not consider that an adjustment for deterrence is
required.
Costs
22. Having regard Ms Nightingale’s financial position Executive Counsel has determined
that she should make a contribution of £10,000 to the costs of this matter.

Annex 1 – ICAEW Code of Ethics 2020 definitions

Professional accountant in business
A professional accountant working in areas such as commerce, industry, service, the public
sector, education, the not-for-profit sector, or in regulatory or professional bodies, who might
be an employee, contractor, partner, director (executive or nonexecutive), owner-manager or
volunteer.

Professional accountant in public practice
A professional accountant, irrespective of functional classification (for example, audit, tax or
consulting) in a firm that provides professional services. The term “professional accountant in
public practice” is also used to refer to a firm of professional accountants in public practice.

7
Annex 2 – ICAEW definition of public practice

You are engaged in public practice if you are a principal or are held out as a principal in:
a) a public practitioner; or
b) the parent of a public practitioner; or
c) an entity which is a principal of a public practitioner.

You are a principal if you are:
a) a member in sole practice
b) a salaried or equity partner of a partnership, a member of a limited liability partnership
(designated and non-designated members), a statutory (de jure) director, a de facto director
or a shadow director of a company; or
c) a member ‘held out’ as a principal.
